sections.h2: Who does what in Flagler County
sections.html:
Value is the Property Appraiser's job. Notices and payments belong to the Tax Collector. The rates come from whichever bodies levy on your parcel, among them the county commission, the school board and each city commission. If a deed needs recording or a parcel is headed to auction, that is the circuit court clerk.

At flaglertax.gov you will find pages for property taxes, tangible personal property, tourist development tax, business tax receipts and veteran benefits. Anything about a value, exemption or classification goes to the Flagler County Property Appraiser, who can give you current forms and filing dates.

sections.h2: How the bill is built and mailed
sections.html:
Taxes here are billed in arrears. The tax year is the calendar year, and the bills for real estate and for tangible personal property are mailed October 31, with payment opening November 1.

Behind that mailing is a fixed sequence:

  • The appraiser finishes the roll by assigning values and applying exemptions.
  • That certified roll is handed to the Tax Collector.
  • Flat non-ad valorem assessments, which have nothing to do with value, are merged in and print on the same notice.
  • The finished notice is mailed to the last address the roll holds for you.

If a servicer pays from escrow, it requests the bill under the Tax Collector's criteria, and your copy is only for your information.

The real estate bill is not the only account the Tax Collector keeps. Landlords and anyone selling business property should know about these.

  • Tangible personal property tax, charged on furnishings and equipment that a rental or business uses.
  • Tourist development tax, owed on short stays in a rental.
  • Business tax receipts for operating a business in the county.
  • Online payment of tax bills.

Winding down a rental? Have the office confirm each account is paid and closed. A leftover balance can surface well after the deed is recorded.

Pay through the official online payment page, not a link that arrives by text or email, since fraudulent texts have circulated.

A missing bill does not excuse the tax. Under section 197.122, which the Tax Collector cites, the owner is expected to learn what is due and pay before delinquency.

People who have moved out, landlords whose tenants pick up the mail and heirs at a house with an old address are the ones caught most often. Lobbies may close at 4 p.m. when crowded. If November ends with nothing in your mailbox, look up the account online and give the Property Appraiser a current mailing address.

sections.h2: The Flagler tax year at a glance
sections.html:
Florida's statewide calendar governs here, and Flagler's offices carry out each step.

Annual property tax dates
DateStep
January 1Property is assessed as of this day
March 1Exemption filings due
April 1Business and rental equipment returns
AugustProposed-tax notice mailed
25 days after the noticeValue petition window
September and OctoberMillage hearings
NovemberBills and early-payment discount
April 1 followingDelinquent

Pay in November and the discount is 4 percent; it drops a point each month until it reaches 1 percent in February.

You can ask for either one, and both requests go to the Tax Collector. For installments the date is May 1 of the assessment year. For deferral you file Form DR-570 by March 31 of the following year.

A homestead owner who defers puts off whatever part of the tax exceeds a slice of household income, 5 percent for most people and 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. The Tax Collector may or may not take partial payments ahead of delinquency; that is its call. The May installment date falls long before any bill is mailed, so phone the office and learn how Flagler handles its plan before you build around it.

sections.h2: Does the assessment cap follow the house?
sections.html:
No. Your buyer is assessed at full just value. Title changes reset a parcel the following January, spousal transfers being among the exceptions, so the capped figure you enjoyed does not pass on.

As long as you keep the homestead, assessed value can climb each year only by 3 percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is smaller; the 2026 figure on the state chart is 2.7 percent. Should you buy another Florida home, part of that savings can be ported if you claim it within three years. The homestead and portability forms both go to the Property Appraiser by March 1.

The Tax Collector's site has a veteran benefits page, but the Property Appraiser handles the exemptions themselves. Florida's list is short.

  • $5,000 off assessed value for a disabled former servicemember whose rating is 10 percent or more.
  • A homestead discount that follows the VA rating, for an owner 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • An exemption based on deployment, claimed on Form DR-501M.

Find out from the Property Appraiser what proof each one needs, and carry your discharge or VA rating papers when you go.

sections.h2: When a parcel reaches a tax deed auction
sections.html:
Two years after a certificate is issued, the holder can apply for a deed and the clerk puts the parcel up at public auction. The Tax Collector compiles whom to notify: the titleholder, mortgagees, lienholders, the party assessed and any recorded contract buyer.

  • Whoever bids highest puts down a deposit that cannot be refunded, the greater of 5 percent of the bid or $200.
  • Everything else, including stamps and recording costs, is owed inside 24 hours, weekends and holidays excluded.
  • If nobody buys the parcel, it lands on the county's lands-available list.

Selling ahead of the auction lets you redeem out of the proceeds. The redemption figure keeps growing with interest, so ask the Flagler Tax Collector for a current one.

Whatever is owed on the parcel comes out of your sale proceeds, handled by the closing agent. Request the balance from the Tax Collector's office. Deed stamps are collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded, at 70 cents per $100 of price statewide.

A certificate on the parcel does not block a sale. It simply gets paid off at the table so the buyer ends up with clean title.

A few days before closing, give the title agent your ID, deed and latest tax bill. Then ask to see a draft settlement statement and make sure its tax line matches the figure the collector quoted for the payment date. When April 1 is close, a cash buyer who skips lender delays can be a real help.

faqs.q: When does Flagler County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: Right around the start of November. The mailing date for real estate and tangible personal property bills is October 31, and you can start paying November 1.

faqs.q: What if I never receive my Flagler County tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, the tax is still owed. Section 197.122 leaves it to the owner to find the amount and pay before delinquency, so call the Tax Collector and the Property Appraiser.

faqs.q: Can I defer Flagler County property tax?
faqs.a: If you have a homestead, apply on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year. What can be deferred is the tax over 5 percent of household income, or over 3 percent if you are a permanent resident 65 or older.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap transfer to the buyer of my Flagler County house?
faqs.a: No, a sale puts the property back at just value on the next January 1. Part of your cap may be portable to a new Florida homestead.

faqs.q: Who sets Flagler County millage rates?
faqs.a: Each levying body sets its own: the county, the school board, the cities and other authorities. The Property Appraiser deals only with value.
